items.question: Which sample each sound id is; are the weapon pickup sounds the reload samples?
items.scenario: slot 10 (level 1): walk to the start door and press Use; fire the pistol 19 times through a reload; every weapon and its ammunition poked in, weapon change, fire and grenade per weapon; teleport onto the battery pickup; teleport in front of the switch panel (type 0x18) and press Use. Slot 4 (level 14): pistol fire at a wall; a lift (no activation). Execute breakpoints on sound_play, sound_play_at, play_menu_sound and voice_play record a0 and the caller. Disc: SFX bank headers parsed and every entry hashed and decoded to WAV.
items.observation: Door: 0x2a from door_task_closed+0x64 when the door starts (frame 30), 0x2b from door_task_opening+0x40 60 frames later when it is fully open. Switch: 0x5c from level_object_activate+0xa4 and switch_panel_task+0x2d8 on the Use press. Battery: 0x28 from pickups_task+0x24c. Pistol reload (15 -> 12 ammo + 1 clip) plays no sound at all. Weapon scripts (frame tables with SPRITE_COMMAND_SOUND words in .text 0x80055930..0x80055c20): pulse rifle fire 0x8106; grenade launch 0x8107 (with pulse_grenade_launch's 0x08); shotgun 0x8110 (fire) then 0x810f mid-animation (pump); pistol 0x810d; flamethrower 0x810a at frame 1 and loop script 0x810b; smart gun fire 0x8113 and a second script with 0x8112. Ids 0x05 and 0x0c occur in no script. Bank hashing: 0x5c, 0x5e, 0x5f and 0x6c are the same sample in every bank that has them; 0x2a/0x2b have one variant per section group (SECT1x, SECT2x, SECT3x; SECT3x banks have no 0x2b). 0x6c exists only in the 131, 211, 212 and 232 banks. Lifts did not move in the level-14 run (Use on the lift does nothing; lifts are trigger-driven), so 0x5e/0x5f rest on lift_task_* and the bank evidence.

recommended_name.0x2b: SOUND_DOOR_STOP (keep; SOUND_DOOR_OPENED is also fitting: retail plays it when the door reaches open and when it finishes closing)
recommended_name.0x07: SOUND_GRENADE_LAUNCHER_LOAD (or keep SOUND_GRENADES_PICKUP; the sample is the launcher's handling sound)

items.confidence: high for the door, switch, pickup and weapon-script observations and for 'pickup sounds are not reload samples' (no reload sound exists); medium for the new handling names (what the sample sounds like was judged from the script position and the decoded waveform, not by listening); medium for 0x5e/0x5f/0x6c (not played in a run)

items.question: What reads Sprite.flags 0x01 (SPRITE_FLAG_MARK) and 0x08 (SPRITE_FLAG_CUE)?
items.scenario: static scan of the retail EXE for every lh/lhu of Sprite.flags (+0x36 in Sprite, +0xb6 in Actor, g_player.weapon_sprite absolute) followed by andi with a mask containing the bit; weapon scripts read from RAM (slot 10)
items.observation: 0x01 is read only by the texture upload code: upload_can_queue_pair+0x24/+0x28 and sprite_frame_upload+0x2c (and boss_sprite_frame_upload+0x28). With the bit set, sprite_frame_upload unpacks the frame into the g_unpack_buffer staging area through unpack_rle or unpack_lz (chosen by mode) and times it with GetRCnt; with it clear the frame pixels are queued directly. Every weapon firing script sets it (0x8300) before its frames. 0x08 is read only by creature_task+0x5cc (actor.c ACTOR_LEAP: on the cue frame the actor fires a bullet or lobs a grenade, then clears the bit).
items.confidence: high for the readers (exhaustive static scan); medium for PACKED (the branch is clear, the runtime path was not stepped)

items.question: What each level object type depicts
items.scenario: slot 10 (level 1): g_level_objects dumped (44 objects: 8 x 0x14, 15 x 0x17, 16 x 0x19, 2 x 0x18, 1 x 0x1a); the player teleported in front of one of each and screenshots taken (builds/runtime/lo_l1*.png). G0LVL22 (level 22): 13 objects, 10 x 0x14 and 3 x 0x18.
items.observation: 0x17: red drums with yellow/black bands (explosive barrels), in rows. 0x14 (level 1): a low green box on the floor, destroyed by hits, drops a pickup (drop[0] 8..22). 0x19: a tall dark container with yellow hazard markings, same task. 0x18: a wall switch panel with hazard stripes (activation played 0x5c). 0x1a: a wall console (battery switch). Level 22 (the derelict/hive tileset) has only 0x14 and 0x18; the 0x14 model there was not identified on screen. No visited level (1, 11, 14, 22) has 0x20..0x25.
items.confidence: medium (screenshots in dark rooms, one object per type); 0x20..0x25 not reached

items.question: Do doors with facing 2/6 (DOOR_ALONG_Z) run along z?
items.scenario: slot 10 (level 1): g_doors read (6 doors) with their cell pointers; the start door opened and walked through
items.observation: Doors with facing 2 or 6 have flags & 2, facing 0/4 have it clear. Map cells are 16 bytes and a map row is 0x5c0 bytes (92 cells): x steps 1 cell, z steps a row (door 2 vs door 3: dz -9 cells = -0x33c0 bytes; doors 4 vs 5: dx -16 cells = -0x100 bytes). A facing-0/4 door's cells c,a,b,d are 16 bytes apart (adjacent along x); a facing-2/6 door's are 0x5c0 apart (adjacent along z). The player crossed door 0 (facing 2) moving along +x, so its panel spans z.

items.observation: 0x7b (code 0xfe) is a round button with a left-pointing triangle, 0x7d (code 0xfd) the same with a right-pointing triangle, 0x77 (code 0xff) the Cross button (the results screen draws it in 'Press X button to continue').

items.question: g_cheat_flags 0x100 and 0x200 (always set): effect when cleared
items.scenario: static scan of every g_cheat_flags access; slot 10 with the player placed next to awake aliens, 300 frames, flag 0x100 kept vs cleared, execute breakpoints on creature_task's idle test (0x8002f180) and wake store (0x8002f194)
items.observation: menu_task+0x788 sets both (ori 0x300) when a game starts. 0x100 is read by creature_task+0x158 and queen_task+0x10c/+0x1d4: an idle actor (action 0) whose idle_timer is 0 wakes (action 1) only while it is set. Run: kept -> 5 tests, 5 wake-ups, 46 positional (creature) sounds; cleared -> 140 tests, 0 wake-ups, 10 positional sounds. 0x200 is read only by lift_draw+0x4: with it clear lift_draw returns without drawing (static; no lift was on screen when it was cleared on level 1).
items.confidence: high for 0x100 (runtime); medium-high for 0x200 (single static reader, not seen)

items.question: g_game_flags 0x4000 (restored?) and 0x10000 (best grade?): who sets/reads; also 0x400 firing flag or screen flash?
items.scenario: static scan of every g_game_flags access with the following 7-16 instructions; one attempt to enter the 2-1 password (typing went wrong, no runtime result); slot 10 with g_game_flags |= 4 ran level_complete to the results screen
items.observation: 0x4000 is set by load_card_slot+0x70 (memory card load) and password_keyboard_input+0x2d4 (password accepted) and cleared by main+0x1c4 when the level loop starts the level; no instruction tests it. 0x10000 is set only by level_complete when the percentage is >= 85 on the last level of a chapter (grade 3); nothing tests or clears it. 0x400 is set by player_fire (every weapon) and big_explosion_spawn, read by f_3b578+0x114 and cleared by lights_task+0x2a8, which lights the scene: a light flash from muzzle flashes and explosions, not a firing state.
items.confidence: medium-high (complete static writer/reader set; the password path was not run)

items.question: MENU_ENTRY_HEADING: any reader?
items.scenario: static scan for lh/lhu at offset 0 followed by andi with any mask containing 8, in every function
items.observation: run_menu tests MenuEntry.flags with 1, 2, 0x10 and 0x20 only; no menu function tests 8. The only andi 8 after an offset-0 halfword load in the front end is pause_menu_init+0x2d8, on a structure with a field at +0xe (not a MenuEntry).

items.question: g_8cedc (0x1e0-byte buffer): who reads it?
items.scenario: static scan of every gp/lui access; round-2 read watchpoints (title, menus, level load, play, death)
items.observation: The only access in the EXE is the store of heap_alloc(0x1e0) in start_menu_tasks+0x8c; the pointer is never loaded. 0x1e0 = 15 x 32, the size of 15 memory card block titles, but nothing fills it.
items.recommended_name: keep g_8cedc (unused allocation); if a name is wanted, g_menu_unused_buffer (invented)
items.confidence: high that it has no reader; no evidence for a purpose

items.question: The four countdown samples: what each is and when it plays (follows item 19)
items.scenario: round 4 (builds/lane_tools/r4): go.py <level> starts a new game from slot 8 and writes g_level at the first password_store_level call of the level loop (the briefing, map, sample bank and countdown all follow the forced level). Levels 2 (113 Ammunition Dump, 60 s), 9 (155 Security Catwalks, 30 s) and 27 (352 Inorganics 1, 45 s) were run; countdown_task's TASK was found in RAM (callback 0x80037ce0), its seconds poked to 23, and sound_play logged with the task's seconds. Level 2 was also run to 0. The samples decoded from the 113/115/352 SFX banks (builds/runtime/samples) were analysed for duration, pitch track and envelope.
items.observation: countdown_task runs every second video frame and counts 30 of its runs per second, so the HUD number is real seconds. Level 2: 0x65 at 20 and 17, 0x63 at 14, nothing below. Level 9: 0x64 at 20 and 17, 0x63 at 14. Level 27: 0x62 at 20, 17, 14, 11, 8, 5 and 2. At 0 the level ends as completed (GAME_FLAG_LEVEL_COMPLETE): the level-password screen follows and g_level advances (2 -> 3). The briefings call these levels re-arm stops ('we can only hover for 60 seconds', 'before we pull you out'). Audio: 0x62 (352 bank, 2.58 s) is three repeats of one voiced tone pattern (pitch steps 225-470 Hz) with no unvoiced gaps: a synthetic klaxon/alarm, not speech. 0x63 (2.77 s), 0x64 (1.16 s) and 0x65 (0.92 s) have speech-like envelopes (a varying 110-215 Hz voiced pitch broken by noise stretches), so they are most likely spoken warnings; the words were not transcribed (no speech recognition available, not listened to).
readers_writers: countdown_start (60 s; 30 s on level 9; 45 s on levels 27 and 30)
main's level loop: level_complete after GAME_FLAG_LEVEL_COMPLETE

recommended_name.0x62: SOUND_COUNTDOWN_ALARM (the klaxon of levels 22+, every 3 s from 20 s)

items.confidence: high for timing and level selection (runtime); medium for alarm versus voice (signal analysis only)

items.question: Level-object types 0x20..0x25: where do they occur and what are they? (follows item 3)
items.scenario: round 4 (builds/lane_tools/r4): maps.py parses the MAP0 chunk of all 35 LxxxLEV.MAP files with level_parse_map's layout (0x80020e14: a 36-byte header, then vertices 8*n, faces 20*n, cells 16*w*h, layout records 8*n, actor slots 20*n, object records 8*n, level objects 16*n; result builds/runtime/r4_maps.json), checked against RAM on levels 0, 4, 11 and 14 (identical actor slot kinds). Levels 4 (131 Med Lab) and 2 (113) reached with go.py; objects moved out of view by poking LevelObject.position and the screenshots compared.
items.observation: 0x20: level 4 (131: four objects in a ring at x 8704..10752, z -14336..-12288 on floor 1920, rotations 0/1024/2048/-1024, created with flags 1 and state 0) and level 12 (211: 9). 0x21: levels 2 (113: 12), 6 (141: 12), 12 (211: 4), 13 (212: 1), 18 (232: 1). 0x22..0x25: on no level. Moving the four level-4 0x20 objects away did not change the view of the column they surround, and moving all twelve level-2 0x21 objects away did not change two views next to them, so neither model was identified on screen (dark rooms, uncertain camera). The same comparison identified 0x15 on level 2: the black ribbed drums with orange-and-black hazard tops (LEVEL_OBJECT_BLOCK). The 0x20 rotations did not change over 30 frames without a trigger.
readers_writers: level_objects_create (0x20: level_object_spin_task, model 40; 0x21..0x25: level_object_task, model type + 2)

recommended_name.0x22..0x25: unused by every level (cases in the switch only)
recommended_name.0x15: LEVEL_OBJECT_BLOCK: the hazard-topped drums of level 113

items.confidence: high for occurrence (all 35 maps); low for the 0x20/0x21 pictures

items.question: Player.item_flags bit 0x4000: what sets it? (follows item 21)
items.scenario: round 4 (builds/lane_tools/r4): every store to 0x8009a03c in the EXE (lui -0x5fc4 stores, and base+0x68 stores with an or nearby); f_3982c+0x180..0x214 disassembled; item_flags polled on cell types 0, 1, 5, 6, 9 (level 3) and through a hugger cling (level 4)
items.observation: Correction to the question: item_flags is 0x80099fd4+0x68 (0x8009a03c); +0x6c (0x8009a040) is health. Writers: player_controls (f_3bc8c: clears 0x200, sets 0x400), player_task_start+0x28c (clears 0x4180 = 0x4000|0x100|0x80), player_reset (zero) and the matched or-sites (weapons, auto mapper, hugger, control bits). No instruction sets 0x4000. f_3982c plays a footstep when the step phase wraps unless the cell type is 9 (no step sound there), choosing 0x26 when 0x4000 is set, else 0x2c. The bit stayed clear in every scenario.
items.recommended_name: unresolved: a dead alternate-footstep bit (no setter in retail); leave it unnamed, or ITEM_FOOTSTEP_ALT noting 'never set'

items.question: A lift in motion: what starts one, and the lift move/stop sounds
items.scenario: round 4 (builds/lane_tools/r4): level 4 (131): its one lift (Lift at 0x800c656c: width 1, depth 5, low 0, high 68, flags 0x21 UP|RESTS_UP, wait 7, count 0) and every cell trigger whose command chain reaches TRIGGER_LIFT (7) listed from RAM (lifts.py); Lift.count poked to 6, the player teleported onto trigger 15's cell (64, 13), sounds logged
items.observation: Lifts are started by cell triggers, not the Use button: each TRIGGER_LIFT / TRIGGER_LIFT_LAST command adds its amount to Lift.count (lift_trigger), and lift_task_wait starts the lift once count >= wait. On level 4 seven separate one-charge triggers each add 1 (several sit in chains with TRIGGER_SWITCH and TRIGGER_DOOR_POWER, i.e. behind switch panels) and the lift needs 7, so it moves only after the whole sequence. With count 6, stepping onto the trigger cell gave 'Lift activated' and 0x5e from lift_task_wait+0x9c at frame 0; the platform lowered 68 height steps (position.vy 2192 -> 16) and 0x5f came from lift_task_lower+0x98 at frame 136 when it reached low; flags became 0xa4 (DOWN|RESTS_UP|COUNTED) and count went back to 0.
items.confidence: high (runtime; the count was pre-poked to skip six switches)

items.question: A wall shatter: what triggers it?
items.scenario: round 4 (builds/lane_tools/r4): level 4 (131): the player teleported in front of wall object 2 (type 0x1c, state 16, 2 x 1 cells) and the pistol fired; breakpoints on the sound functions and level_object_tick
items.observation: The first pistol bullet to reach the wall's cell called level_object_tick(2, 0x10) from the bullet hit code (f_24140+0x194): the bullet's damage (16) used up the wall's state (16), which arms it with hits = (random & 7) + 1. 16 frames later block_object_task+0x130 played 0x6c at the wall (wall_shatter) and wall panels fell, each playing 0x6d from particles_task as it landed. A face-hugger waited behind the wall. explosion_damage arms walls as well. Walls (0x1c) are on levels 4 (131: 14), 12 (211: 2) and 13 (212: 15); the 232 bank carries 0x6c but level 232 has no 0x1c object.
items.recommended_name: SOUND_WALL_SHATTER (keep); LEVEL_OBJECT_WALL is a breakable wall (state = hit points)

items.question: MapCell.type values from the player constants lane: 5 and 9 (slow), 20 and 25 (player_move_x/_z thresholds), 6 (automap)
items.scenario: round 4 (builds/lane_tools/r4): cell types (+0xa) counted in all 35 MAP files and in RAM; teleports onto each type on level 3 (122) with the cell under the player (Player.cell, 0x8009a038) read back; static readers
items.observation: 9: only levels 3 (122 Recreation Rooms, 231 cells) and 17 (231 Mining and Smelting, 853 cells). Shots hitting a type-9 cell spray slow impact sparks (impact_spray selection 1; type 8 selection 2), falling particles stop 384 above the floor in type 9 and 256 in type 8 (they sink into it), footsteps are silent on 9 (f_3982c), and the player moves at half speed on 5 and 9 unless boots_timer runs. No damage was taken standing on 9 for 30 frames. So 9 is a deep liquid and 8 (levels 24, 26) a shallow one. 5 (19 levels) is a slow floor with normal footsteps and no splash. The dark rooms made the screenshots uninformative. 6: on every level. Level 4's door-trigger cells (64, 12..15) are type 6 with ceiling == floor (80/80). Actor code tests 'type == 6 && ceiling - value < 4', particles skip the ceiling clamp on 6, and the automap colours 6 with palette 5 (green), so 6 is a door cell (its ceiling is the door). 20..24 stop both player and actors (20 is the common solid wall cell, about 1000 per level, and a projectile entering a type-20 cell explodes in particle_hit_floor_or_ceiling). 25..44 pass the player's test (type < 20 or 25..44) but actors treat 20..44 as blocked. 45 and up is a separate class in the actor code.
